terms.title: Terms of Service

list.item1: "OfferMarket" means OfferMarket B.V., registered in the Netherlands.
list.item2: "Platform" means the OfferMarket web application and related services.
list.item3: "Worker" means a professional who creates a profile to receive offers from employers.
list.item4: "Employer" means a company or individual who sends offers to workers through the platform.
list.item5: "Offer" means a proposal sent by an employer to a worker containing employment terms.
list.item6: "User" means any person who uses the platform, including workers and employers.

s2.title: 2. Acceptance of Terms
s2.p1: By creating an account or using the OfferMarket platform, you agree to these Terms of Service and our Privacy Policy. If you do not agree, you must not use the platform.
s2.p2: These terms are governed by Dutch law. For dispute resolution, see Section 23 (Dispute Resolution and Governing Law).

s3.title: 3. Account Registration
s3.intro: You must register to use the platform. By registering you represent and warrant that:

list.item1: You are at least 18 years old
list.item2: You provide accurate and complete information
list.item3: You will keep your information up to date
list.item4: You will maintain the security of your account credentials
list.item5: You will not create multiple accounts or impersonate others

workersList.item1: You create a professional profile that employers can discover
workersList.item2: Your profile is anonymous until you accept an offer — your name, email, and contact details are hidden
workersList.item3: You may receive offers from verified employers
workersList.item4: You are not obligated to accept any offer
workersList.item5: Upon accepting an offer, your identity is revealed to the employer for contract purposes

employersList.item1: You can search anonymous worker profiles based on skills, experience, and preferences
employersList.item2: You can send offers to workers with employment terms
employersList.item3: You must be a registered business (KvK number required)
employersList.item4: Offer terms must comply with Dutch employment law
employersList.item5: Upon offer acceptance, the worker's identity is revealed for contract purposes

s5.title: 5. Billing & Payments
s5.p1: Employers are charged an introduction fee when a worker accepts an offer. Payment terms are as specified in the invoice. All prices include VAT where applicable.
s5.p2: Late payments may incur interest at the statutory rate (Wet Handelscrediteuren). OfferMarket reserves the right to suspend accounts with overdue invoices.

list.item1: Use the platform for any unlawful purpose
list.item2: Discriminate against workers based on protected characteristics
list.item3: Share or distribute worker personal data outside the platform without consent
list.item4: Attempt to de-anonymize workers before offer acceptance
list.item5: Create fake profiles or misrepresent your identity
list.item6: Use automated systems (bots, scrapers) to extract data from the platform
list.item7: Circumvent the platform to avoid introduction fees
list.item8: Upload special category data (nationality, health, union membership) into profile free-text fields

s7.title: 7. Intellectual Property
s7.p1: The platform, its design, and its content (excluding user-generated content) are owned by OfferMarket B.V. You retain ownership of your profile content and offers. By posting content, you grant OfferMarket a limited, non-exclusive license to display it on the platform.

s8.title: 8. Privacy & Data Protection
s8.intro: Our processing of personal data is governed by our Privacy Policy, which forms part of these terms. Key points:

list.item1: We process your data lawfully, fairly, and transparently (AVG Art. 5)
list.item2: We only collect data necessary for the purposes stated
list.item3: Worker profiles are anonymous by default — identity is only revealed upon offer acceptance
list.item4: Work authorization status is special category data processed only with explicit consent
list.item5: You can exercise your AVG rights through the Privacy Dashboard

s9.title: 9. Liability
s9.p1: OfferMarket acts as an intermediary connecting workers and employers. We are not a party to any employment contract between users. OfferMarket is not liable for:

list.item1: The quality, legality, or accuracy of offers or profiles
list.item2: Any employment disputes between workers and employers
list.item3: Losses arising from reliance on information on the platform

s9.p2: Our total liability is limited to the fees you paid in the 12 months preceding the claim.

s10.title: 10. Force Majeure
s10.p1: Neither party shall be liable for any failure or delay in performing its obligations under these terms where such failure or delay results from circumstances beyond its reasonable control, including but not limited to: natural disasters, pandemics, war, terrorism, riots, strikes or other labour disputes, fire, flood, interruption or failure of internet service providers, telecommunications networks, power utilities, or cloud infrastructure providers, and governmental actions or orders.
s10.p2: If a force majeure event continues for more than 30 consecutive days, either party may terminate these terms with immediate effect by written notice to the other party, without liability for such termination.
s10.p3: OfferMarket B.V. will make reasonable efforts to notify users of the nature and expected duration of any force majeure event affecting the platform via email or a notice on the platform.

s11.title: 11. Termination
s11.p1pre: You may close your account at any time through the

s11.p2: OfferMarket may suspend or terminate accounts that violate these terms, with prior notice where possible.

s12.title: 12. Changes
s12.p1: We may update these terms. Significant changes will be communicated via email. Continued use of the platform after changes constitutes acceptance.

s13.title: 13. Illegal Content Reporting (DSA Art. 16)
s13.intro: Under the Digital Services Act (Regulation EU 2022/2065), you have the right to notify us of content on OfferMarket that you believe to be illegal. Our notice-and-action mechanism is available at:
s13.statusNote: You can also check the status of a report at Report Status.

list.item1: You may report content anonymously by providing an email address for acknowledgment.
list.item2: You must provide a sufficiently detailed explanation of why you believe the content is illegal (DSA Art. 16(3)(a)).
list.item3: You must confirm that your notice is submitted in good faith (DSA Art. 16(3)(d)).
list.item4: We will acknowledge your report without undue delay and inform you of the decision.

s14.title: 14. Content Moderation (DSA Art. 14)
s14.intro: OfferMarket uses a combination of human review and automated systems to moderate content on the platform. Our content moderation policies and procedures include:

list.item1: Human review — All content reports are assessed by trained staff members.
list.item2: Automated detection — We use automated systems to detect potentially illegal content (e.g., known illegal patterns, spam detection). Automated actions are reviewed by a human within 24 hours.
list.item3: Notice-and-action procedure — We follow the procedure described in Section 12 when processing illegal content reports.
list.item4: Statement of reasons — When we restrict content, we provide the affected user with a clear statement of reasons (DSA Art. 17).

s15.title: 15. Statement of Reasons (DSA Art. 17)
s15.intro: When we restrict content on the platform (removal, visibility limitation, account suspension, etc.), we will provide the affected user with a statement of reasons that includes:

list.item1: The type of restriction applied (removal, visibility limitation, geo-blocking, etc.)
list.item2: The factual circumstances and reasons for the decision
list.item3: The source of the decision (user report, own investigation, authority order, trusted flagger)
list.item4: Whether automated means were used in the decision
list.item5: The legal or contractual ground for the restriction
list.item6: The territorial scope of the restriction
list.item7: Information on how to submit a complaint (see Section 17)

s16.title: 16. Referral to Authorities (DSA Art. 18)
s16.p1: Where we have reasonable grounds to believe that a report concerns an offence involving a threat to the life or safety of persons, we will promptly refer the matter to the relevant law enforcement authorities in the Netherlands.
s16.p2: Reports involving suspected child safety concerns or terrorism-related content are escalated as a matter of priority.

s17.title: 17. Complaint-Handling (DSA Art. 20)
s17.intro: If you disagree with a content moderation decision, you may submit a complaint through our internal complaint-handling system. Complaints are:

list.item2: Handled by qualified staff who were not involved in the original decision

s17.p2: You may also seek out-of-court dispute settlement through certified bodies as provided for under DSA Art. 21, once such bodies are available.

s18.title: 18. Misuse of Notice-and-Action (DSA Art. 23)
s18.intro: Submitting manifestly unfounded notices or notices containing manifestly illegal content may result in:

list.item3: Temporary suspension of your ability to submit reports
list.item4: Permanent ban from the notice-and-action mechanism

s18.p2: Misuse warnings are lifted after a reasonable period, provided no further misuse occurs.

s19.title: 19. Trader Traceability (DSA Art. 30)
s19.intro: As an online marketplace, OfferMarket collects and verifies information about employers (traders) who use the platform. Before an employer can publish offers, we collect:

list.item6: Self-certification that the trader complies with applicable EU rules

s19.p2: This information is displayed on employer profiles and is stored for 6 months after the end of the contractual relationship, in accordance with DSA Art. 30(4).

s20.title: 20. Transparency Reporting (DSA Arts. 15, 24)
s20.intro: OfferMarket publishes transparency reports on content moderation activities, available at:
s20.p2: These reports include information on the number of notices received, content removed, accounts suspended, response times, and the use of automated means for content moderation.

s21.title: 21. Single Point of Contact
s21.intro: For all matters related to the Digital Services Act, you may contact:
s21.company: OfferMarket B.V. — DSA Single Point of Contact
s21.urgentNote: For urgent matters involving threats to life or safety, contact the relevant law enforcement authorities directly.

s22.title: 22. Severability
s22.p1: If any provision of these terms is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, such provision shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid and enforceable, or if modification is not possible, shall be severed from these terms. The invalidity of any provision shall not affect the validity or enforceability of any other provision, which shall remain in full force and effect.
s22.p2: These terms shall be interpreted so as to best effect the parties' intentions, and any provisions that are found to be invalid or unenforceable shall be replaced by valid provisions that most closely match the intent of the original provisions.
s22.p3: This applies in particular to the limitation of liability provisions in Section 9, which shall be reduced to the maximum extent permitted under applicable mandatory law, including but not limited to Dutch Book 6 Article 7:658 (employer liability) and Article 6:248 BW (reasonableness and fairness).

s23.title: 23. Dispute Resolution and Governing Law
s23.governingP: These terms are governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Netherlands, without regard to its conflict of law provisions.
s23.consumerIntro: If you are a consumer as defined in Dutch law (BW 6:248c), the following applies to you:

consumerList.item1: Out-of-court dispute resolution — Before initiating court proceedings, you may submit a complaint to the Geschillencommissie (Disputes Committee) via degeschillencommissie.nl. The Geschillencommissie issues a binding ruling on disputes concerning the interpretation or performance of these terms.
consumerList.item2: EU Online Dispute Resolution — The European Commission provides an online dispute resolution (ODR) platform at ec.europa.eu/consumers/odr, which consumers may use to resolve disputes arising from online services without recourse to court (EU Directive 2013/11/EU).
consumerList.item3: Mandatory consumer rights — Nothing in these terms deprives you of the protection afforded by mandatory provisions of Dutch law or the law of your habitual residence as a consumer. Where mandatory consumer protection laws in your country of residence provide greater protection than Dutch law, those laws shall prevail.

s23.businessP: If you are a business user (employer), disputes arising out of or in connection with these terms shall be submitted to the competent court in Amsterdam, the Netherlands (Rechtbank Amsterdam).
s23.internalP: Before initiating formal dispute resolution, you may file a complaint with OfferMarket via legal@offermarket.nl. We will acknowledge your complaint within 5 business days and provide a substantive response within 30 calendar days.
s23.limitationP: Claims arising from these terms must be brought within the statutory limitation period under Dutch law (generally 5 years from the date the claim becomes due and the creditor is aware of the relevant facts, per BW 3:306), unless a shorter period is provided by mandatory law.

cookies.title: Cookie Policy

s1.title: 1. What Are Cookies
s1.p1: Cookies are small text files stored on your device when you visit our website. They help us provide you with a better experience by remembering your preferences, enabling essential functionality, and helping us understand how you use our platform.

s2.title: 2. Legal Basis
s2.p1: This cookie policy is made in accordance with Article 11.7a of the Dutch Telecommunicatiewet (Telecommunicatiewet), which implements Article 5(3) of the ePrivacy Directive (Directive 2002/58/EC, as amended by Directive 2009/136/EC).
s2.p2: Under this law, we are required to obtain your informed and unambiguous consent before storing or accessing non-essential cookies on your device. Essential cookies (strictly necessary for the functioning of the website) are exempt from this requirement.
s2.p3: Your consent is freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous. You may withdraw your consent at any time through the cookie banner, the Cookie Settings link in the footer, or our Privacy Dashboard. Withdrawing consent is as easy as giving it.
s2.p4: Consent is valid for a maximum of 13 months, after which you will be asked to renew it. We store your consent preference with a timestamp so we can verify compliance.
s2.p5: Cookies are small text files stored on your device when you visit our website. They help us provide you with a better experience by remembering your preferences, enabling essential functionality, and helping us understand how you use our platform.

essential.title: Essential Cookies
essential.description: These cookies are strictly necessary for the website to function. They cannot be disabled.

analytics.title: Analytics Cookies
analytics.description: These cookies help us understand how visitors interact with our website. We use PostHog for anonymized analytics. These cookies require your consent.

row1.purpose: PostHog analytics — page views, feature usage

marketing.title: Marketing Cookies
marketing.description: These cookies are used to track visitors across websites for advertising purposes. We do not currently use any marketing cookies, but this category is available if we introduce them in the future.
marketing.italicNote: No marketing cookies are currently in use.

s4.title: 4. How to Manage Cookies
s4.intro: You can manage your cookie preferences at any time:

list.item1: Through our Privacy Dashboard — consent management section
list.item2: By clicking the cookie banner that appears on your first visit
list.item3: Using the Cookie Settings link in the page footer
list.item4: Through your browser settings — most browsers allow you to block or delete cookies

s4.p2: Please note that disabling essential cookies may prevent the platform from functioning correctly.

s5.title: 5. PostHog Analytics
s5.intro: We use PostHog for product analytics. PostHog is only activated after you give explicit consent per Article 11.7a of the Telecommunicatiewet. When analytics cookies are enabled:

list.item1: Page views and feature usage are tracked
list.item2: IP addresses are collected but we configure PostHog to mask them
list.item3: Data is stored on EU-based servers
list.item4: We have a Data Processing Agreement with PostHog
list.item5: You can withdraw your consent at any time through the cookie banner, Cookie Settings link, or Privacy Dashboard
list.item6: When consent is withdrawn, all tracking stops immediately

s6.title: 6. Local Storage
s6.intro: In addition to cookies, we use browser local storage for:

list.item1: Authentication tokens — to maintain your login session
list.item2: User preferences — such as theme and notification settings
list.item3: Cookie consent preferences — to remember your choices

s6.p2: Local storage data is not shared with third parties and does not track you across websites.

s7.title: 7. Changes to This Policy
s7.p1: We may update this cookie policy from time to time. Changes will be reflected in the "Last updated" date at the top. If we introduce new non-essential cookies, we will seek your consent again through the cookie banner.

s8.title: 8. Contact
s8.p1: For questions about our use of cookies, contact our Data Protection Officer at dpo@offermarket.nl.
